paired_method: Same process; common cache and page textures; renderer order alternates by scene; warmup discarded. One pair per scene.

mesh.excludes: touch hardware sampling, compositor presentation, display scanout

shader.excludes: touch hardware sampling, compositor presentation, display scanout

visual_assessment.same_geometry_intent: Spine-anchored row curl with corner control and perspective. Shader analytically inverts horizontal projection with three vertical corrections.
differences: Analytic shadow instead of blurred path shadow.
No 0.6 logical pixel mesh outline stroke.
Different texture interpolation and approximate inverse; not pixel-identical.
Curved material boundaries currently have no explicit analytic antialiasing.

validation.physical_gestures: Both routes: 5 forward, 2 backward, 1 short cancel; final page 4.

recommendation: Continue shader route as the next prototype baseline. Keep mesh for visual comparisons; do not integrate into production readers yet.
limitations: Synthetic typography and PNG fixtures; real PDFium rendering of a simple generated PDF.
No production chapter layout, EPUB capture, CBZ extraction, disk I/O, selection or progress integration.
RGBA bytes exclude PDF/native/transient/cached GPU allocations; RSS is whole-process memory.
Pipeline budget exceedance is not measured dropped-frame rate or input-to-display latency.
No Apple Books side-by-side comparison; row curl is not a physical paper solver.
Shader uses an approximate vertical inverse, analytic shadows, and no mesh edge stroke. It is not pixel-equivalent to the mesh.
Only one Android device; iOS and desktop shader performance not tested.
Initial separate shader run showed PDF raster P95 8.702/8.845 ms; this did not reproduce in the same-process pair. Raw standalone trials retained; frequency/scheduling variability remains.
Input shader max event-to-raster-finish was 43.535 ms versus mesh 20.478 ms. Cold pipeline warmup and rare-tail behavior need profiling; shader latency does not improve at every percentile.
Input dispatch-to-paint P95 increased from 4.825 to 7.304 ms despite lower event-to-raster-finish P95. Both stages are retained, not treated as universal improvement.
One adjacent input session per renderer; software input injection excludes hardware touch sampling and display scanout.
No Apple Books parity or side-by-side comparison; analytic shadows and material-edge treatment require further visual work.
